A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete 15-page v1 and 14-page v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Relocated proofs and renumbered appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 training results, gradient analyses, component ablations, and hyperparameter experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds three-run summary results in Table 5 and an ECDF-based evaluation case study in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The hard-sample discarding, radius-based reweighting, spherical adaptive attack, and combined training procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. The new ECDF material concerns evaluation rather than changes to model training or inference.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 classification with the same noise-level coverage. The added certification-budget case study reuses this coverage; it introduces no new dataset, population, or input-domain scenario.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons preserve their baseline memberships, including Gaussian, MACER, SmoothAdv, Consistency, SmoothMix, and CAT-RS in Table 2. Appendix B reuses Gaussian, Consistency, and CAT-RS for its new case study. Newly cited diffusion and adaptive methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds an evaluation at N = 100 and α = 0.01, deriving certified-accuracy curves from an ECDF estimated with N = 100,000 without further model inference. The original training settings and main certification protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a case study examining how ECDF information supports evaluation under a different certification budget, with new Figures 7–8. Existing component, hyperparameter, and attack-variant ablations are retained; v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 9.

E5.justification: v2 Table 5 and Appendix E.1 newly report means and standard deviations from three independent runs with different seeds for the proposed method at all three noise levels. This is a limited uncertainty check; baseline variability and formal significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation values are retained. New Table 5 reports mean ACRs of 0.5613, 0.7587, and 0.8434 at σ = 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0. Appendix B adds derived results, including expected certified accuracy 0.316 at radius 0.5 under N = 100 and α = 0.01.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and their proofs are retained, with the proofs moved to Appendix A. Sections 4.1–4.2 add a worked counterexample showing ranking reversals at certification budgets 50, 100, and 200. Section 7 and Appendix B add distribution-dominance and conversion reasoning under a large-N approximation.

C1.justification: The central critique of ACR and the easy-sample training contributions remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the recommendation from seeking better metrics to discontinuing ACR, and explicitly promote best certified accuracy across noise levels and the empirical distribution of p_A.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops the interpretation of budget-dependent rankings and distinguishes recommendations for fixed versus varying certification settings. Section 7 expands the alternative-metric discussion, while Appendix B explicitly limits ECDF conversion to sufficiently accurate population estimates and leaves corrections for small-N estimates unresolved.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents binary search for the required p_A, ECDF lookup, and reverse conversion from certified-accuracy curves, explaining how to reuse results without model inference. The original training details, PGD updates, and Table 4 hyperparameters are retained in Appendix C.

R1.justification: v2 adds Carlini et al. (2022), Xiao et al. (2022), Zhang et al. (2023), Jeong and Shin (2024), and Nurlanov et al. (2023). These contextualize prior avoidance or continued use of ACR and adaptive noise-level approaches; the original related-work survey largely remains.

P1.justification: Selected passages in the abstract, introduction, and discussion are rewritten, several headings change, and terminology is edited. Proofs move to a new appendix, existing appendices are reorganized, and an impact statement is added. The main section sequence and most methodological prose remain.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two, resizing and repositioning figures, tables, and algorithms throughout. Several paired plots become vertically stacked. v2 also adds Figures 7–8 and Table 5 while retaining and renumbering the older appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The budget-dependent counterexample, practical ECDF case study, and three-seed reporting improve explanation and transparency. The gain is limited: baseline uncertainty remains absent, and the unchanged claim of consistently superior ACR is not established by the new statistics—at σ = 0.25, Table 5 reports 0.5613 ± 0.0022 versus CAT-RS's 0.562 in Table 2.
